source_text: Tu autem qui supra dixeras, omnes ire in condemnationem, qua testimonium fronte posuisti, quo pronuntiatur ire alius in honorem, alius in contumeliam?
pass_a_gloss: You however who had said above, that all go into condemnation, with what forehead did you place a testimony, by which it is pronounced that another goes unto honor, another unto insult?
pass_b_english: But you, who had said above that everyone goes into condemnation, with what effrontery did you quote a testimony declaring that one goes to honor and another to dishonor?

choices.why: Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
